channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Federal immigration agent shoots and injures man in Austin, Texas
item.description: A federal immigration agent shot and injured a Venezuelan immigrant during an operation in Austin, Texas, officials said.

item.title: What to know as world leaders converge at the United Nations this week
item.description: United Nations head António Guterres returns to New York for his final U.N. General Assembly as diplomacy falters over wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, and the global body faces deep divisions.

item.title: Diesel -- the fuel the U.S. economy runs on -- hits record high
item.description: Diesel prices continue setting records, now above $6.50 a gallon. That could mean higher prices not just for truckers, but for everyone.

item.title: How a national farm leader is dealing with record diesel prices
item.description: John Boyd Jr., president of the National Black Farmers Association, says soaring diesel costs are deepening a farm crisis as farmers face sharply higher fuel costs in the middle of harvest season.

item.title: Is homegrown food safer?
item.description: Home gardening is getting a boost in part from fears of foodborne illness. Experts say what is, or is not, safer when it comes to home grown.

item.title: Conflicts over Israel divide some American Jews for Yom Kippur
item.description: For many Jews, Yom Kippur is one of the holiest days of the year. But as internal conflicts over Israel divide some American Jews, some are staying away from synagogues and family gatherings.
